skill_outcomes.outcome_description: Understand fundamental concepts of microeconomics including supply and demand, market equilibrium, consumer behavior, production functions, cost structures, market structures, international trade, and government roles.
Analyze the forces that determine market equilibrium, understand elasticity, and apply these concepts to real-world scenarios.
Explain how consumers make decisions based on budget constraints and utility maximization.
Understand the relationship between inputs and outputs, scale economies, and cost structures in production processes.
Differentiate between perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, and oligopoly, and analyze their implications for business strategy.
Examine the role of international trade in economic activities, including comparative advantage, trade policies, and government interventions.
Identify market failures and evaluate the role of government in addressing these failures through regulation and public policy.
Develop skills to conduct research, analyze, synthesize, and generalize basic microeconomic issues.
Demonstrate ability to work independently and collaboratively to solve problems.
Show commitment to class rules, discipline, teamwork, and personal responsibility for assigned tasks.
Develop the ability to learn independently, accumulate experience, and enhance professional expertise.
